Hi all,

I dug into the session logs and reproduced the redirect behavior. Root cause looks like a cookie domain collision between HarborCraft's corporate SSO domain and the Coupa invite flow. The browser is sending a stale session cookie that causes the Coupa frontend to redirect to the IdP sign-in endpoint instead of rendering the Accept flow.

What I tried:
- Replayed the invite token (same behavior in a standard Chrome profile)
- Cleared the Coupa-related cookies and retried — Accept shows up
- Recreated an invite with a fresh token and tested in incognito — works consistently

Short-term workarounds (pick one):
1) Use a private/incognito window to accept the invite (fastest).
2) Open the invite link in a different browser that hasn't authenticated with HarborCraft SSO.
3) If you prefer, we can regenerate the invite token and paste a direct accept URL — I've created a fresh token and included it in the attached file invite-regenerated.txt (one-time use).

I've uploaded session snippets to our internal ticket: https://support.redwood.example/ticket/INC-20261115-3821 and attached the server-side capture (coupa-session-logs.txt) and a sample screenshot (coupa-error-screenshot.png) that Luis sent. We'll follow up with Coupa if we see recurring collisions across customers; for now the incognito/regen approach is lowest friction.

Planned follow-up: I'll add an item to PORTAL-1147 to add a detect-and-invalidate step for known cookie collisions so future invites render the Accept button irrespective of IdP cookies.
